title: Azure Container Instances Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.45 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.45 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:monitor:metric` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.containerinstance/containergroups"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.45_azure_container_instance_45"
| sort -_time
description: ACI containers are short-lived and opaque without platform metrics; monitoring restarts and resource exhaustion preserves burst workloads and integrations.
value: Detecting azure container instances health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Route Azure Monitor metrics for Container Instances to Splunk using the Azure Add-on (Event Hub or metrics export). Enable diagnostic logs for container groups. Normalize `resource_name` to container group. Alert on CPU/memory threshold breaches, exit code non-zero patterns in logs, and restart counts from platform events.
visualization: Line chart (CPU/memory over time), Table (container group, region, state), Bar chart (events by group).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics) with the modular input for `azure:monitor:metric`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Route Azure Monitor metrics for Container Instances to Splunk using the Azure Add-on (Event Hub or metrics export). Enable diagnostic logs for container groups. Normalize `resource_name` to container group. Alert on CPU/memory threshold breaches, exit code non-zero patterns in logs, and restart counts from platform events.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.containerinstance/containergroups"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.45_azure_container_instance_45"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:monitor:metric` in `index=cloud` to detect azure container instances health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_45_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (CPU/memory over time), Table (container group, region, state), Bar chart (events by group)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure container instances health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
